latest.summary: Operating margins for the quarter stood at 14.8%. From a vertical perspective, in Communications, revenues grew 9.5% year-on-year, supported by the ramp-up of the Orange large deal and new strategic engagements. Hi-Tech grew 6.7% year-on-year, supported by new deal wins.
highlights: Operating margins for the quarter stood at 14.8%.
From a vertical perspective, in Communications, revenues grew 9.5% year-on-year, supported by the ramp-up of the Orange large deal and new strategic engagements.
Hi-Tech grew 6.7% year-on-year, supported by new deal wins.
Coming to deal wins, our total deal wins for the quarter were US$1.023 billion.
Communications business grew 6% Q-o-Q, supported by ramp-up of large deals and strategic new engagements.

willEndure: The margin improvement was driven by strong volume growth and Project Fortius savings, partially offset by the wage hikes.
strengths: We generated US$135 million of free cash flow during the quarter.
We reiterate our stance to maintain 90% to 100% free cash flow to PAT on a full-year basis.
weaknesses: Manufacturing revenue declined 3.9% sequentially against a higher prior-quarter base following the accelerated execution of a large European automotive program in the prior quarter, which I'd mentioned last time.
opportunities: In INR terms, profit after tax stood at INR1,586 crores with a PAT margin of 9.8% and expansion of 130 basis points on a Y-o-Y basis.
threats: A sequential revenue headwind associated with the program is expected in Q3 as well, though to a much smaller extent.

prior.summary: Operating margins stood at 14.4%, reflecting sustained execution discipline, operational rigor, and a continuous focus on profitable growth. Moving to deal momentum, we delivered total deal wins of US$1.078 billion. The commercial model is tied to measurable outcomes, roughly 40% fewer tickets, 20% lower mean time to resolution, 30% to 35% reduction in technical debt, and significant productivity improvement over the deal duration.
highlights: Operating margins stood at 14.4%, reflecting sustained execution discipline, operational rigor, and a continuous focus on profitable growth.
Moving to deal momentum, we delivered total deal wins of US$1.078 billion.

The commercial model is tied to measurable outcomes, roughly 40% fewer tickets, 20% lower mean time to resolution, 30% to 35% reduction in technical debt, and significant productivity improvement over the deal duration.
Our total deal wins for the quarter stood at US$1,078 million, up 33.3% Y-o-Y.
EBIT margins for the quarter were at US$238 million with EBIT percent at 14.4%, up 60 bps Q-o-Q and 330 basis points Y-o-Y.

willDo: Based on our pipeline and the ramp-up of recent deal wins, we expect this positive momentum to continue, subject of course to the broader macroeconomic environment.
willEndure: The one sort of headwind that we will have is the fact that we had a one-off in our European auto business in this quarter, which will show some signs of slowdown then in Q2.

As far as the wage piece is concerned, we expect to be able to announce it effective Q2, obviously in a phased fashion which we will be announcing, to our employees in the days to come, so that will be effective, it'll…
strengths: We generated US$167 million of free cash flow during the quarter, up 94% on a Y-o-Y basis.
weaknesses: Technology, media, and entertainment declined 1.7% Q-o-Q on account of continued volatility in the client spend.
So I would say I'm not seeing an outsized or a very large level of client delays or cancellations, and hopefully this is proven by our own large deal track record over the past three quarters.
opportunities: In INR terms, profit after tax is INR1,465 crores with a PAT margin of 9.3% and an expansion of 80 basis points on a Y-o-Y basis.
threats: So I think these were the two headwinds for us coming into Comms for Q1, but despite that, we've delivered, you know, we've delivered a positive year-on-year growth number.
